title: Home care visit verification and billing hold queue
one_liner: One queue for home care visits with missing or mismatched EVV records, held from billing until a coordinator signs off.

practice.name: Cedar Bend Home Care
practice.type: Non-medical home care agency, personal care and companion services
practice.size: 32 caregivers, about 340 visits a week, Medicaid waiver and private-pay clients

persona.name: Marisol Reyes
persona.day_in_the_life: Marisol starts at 7:20am on Monday. Last week's 340 visits sit in three places that don't talk: the scheduling calendar, the caregiver app's clock-in and clock-out events, and the state EVV aggregator's confirmation file. She pastes all three into a reconciliation spreadsheet her predecessor built, filters for blanks and mismatches by hand, and works the list until both deadlines close on Thursday: the caregiver payroll run at 1pm and the Friday Medicaid claim batch. Last week 38 visits came back flagged, and two caregivers were paid late because of it.

problem.current_workflow: Visit data arrives from three systems that don't reconcile: the schedule, the caregiver mobile app, and the state EVV aggregator file. Marisol exports each into a spreadsheet, sorts for missing clock-outs and location mismatches by eye, then calls caregivers and family members to fill in the gaps before the weekly payroll and claim deadlines.
pain_points: A missing clock-out or an out-of-geofence clock-in is only caught when a person reads a spreadsheet
The same visit can look correct in the caregiver app and wrong in the state aggregator, with no single record of truth
Exceptions are worked in the same short week they're due, with no buffer before payroll and claims close
Address and authorization changes don't propagate, so a visit that was actually fine gets flagged anyway
problem.cost_of_pain: Marisol spends 9 to 11 hours a week reconciling visit records by hand, about 130 caregiver hours a week sit on hold until they clear, and roughly $3,100 in wages reaches caregivers after payday. Every Friday claim batch also carries a handful of visits at risk of rejection.

story.before: Monday, 7:20am. Marisol opens the scheduling portal, the caregiver app export, and the state aggregator file side by side and pastes all three into the reconciliation spreadsheet. She filters for blanks and starts working down the list. At 9:40am she reaches a Thursday visit for client H. Pruitt: caregiver Dwayne Ellison clocked in on his phone at 8:02am, there's no clock-out, and the aggregator shows that clock-in 0.4 miles outside the geofence on file. She calls Dwayne (voicemail), calls the family (they confirm he stayed until noon), types a note, and moves on. That was one visit out of 38. Payroll closes Thursday at 1pm.
story.after: Monday, 7:20am. Marisol opens one queue. Last week's visits are already reconciled against the state file, and 38 are waiting with a plain reason next to each: no clock-out recorded, location outside geofence, visit overlaps another visit, service code mismatch. She opens visit #41882, sees that the client's address changed two weeks ago and the profile was never updated, corrects the address, attaches the family's written confirmation, and sends the visit to billing review. By 7:55am she has cleared 14 of the 38; every remaining visit has a named next step and an owner. Payroll and the Friday claim batch both run on time.

edge_case.scenario: Visit #41882 (caregiver Dwayne Ellison, client H. Pruitt, personal care, Thursday 8:00am-12:00pm) has no clock-out recorded, and the clock-in GPS reads 0.4 miles outside the geofence on file. The root cause is a conflicting record: the client moved two apartments over two weeks ago and nobody updated the address or geofence, so one clean four-hour visit is flagged twice.
edge_case.how_handled: The visit sits in the Exceptions queue with the reason 'No clock-out recorded' and a live age in business days computed from the visit date, never written in. Marisol corrects the client address in the record, attaches the family's written confirmation of the four hours, and moves the visit to billing review herself; nothing clears on its own.
edge_case.label: No clock-out recorded

human_checkpoint.what_staff_does: Marisol reviews the corrected visit record, the confirmed hours, and the attached family confirmation, then clicks 'Approve for billing'. Only then does the visit enter the Friday Medicaid claim batch and the caregiver's payroll.

entities.name: Visits
entities.realism_notes: About 86% of visits verify clean on the first pass, roughly 12% come back flagged, and the rest are same-day visits still waiting on the state aggregator file. Flagged visits spread across four plain-language reasons: no clock-out recorded, location outside geofence, visit overlaps another visit, service code mismatch. Service codes are HCPCS personal care codes with the kit's own plain-language labels, e.g. T1019 'personal care, 15-minute unit'. All client and caregiver names are fictional. Visit #41882 is the edge case: caregiver Dwayne Ellison, client H. Pruitt, T1019 personal care, visit_date 4 days ago (a Thursday), scheduled 8:00am-12:00pm, confirmed_hours 4.0, clock_in 8:02am via mobile GPS, clock_out blank, geofence_status 'outside geofence' because the client moved two apartments over two weeks ago and the client profile still lists the old address, verification_status 'flagged', flagged_date 4 days ago, cleared_date blank, exception_reason exactly 'No clock-out recorded', payroll_status 'held' until the billing review step approves it.

entities.name: Caregivers
entities.realism_notes: About 70% personal care aides and 30% companions; weekly scheduled hours range 16-40 with a median near 32; about 90% are enrolled in the mobile app, and the rest clock in by telephone from the client's landline. A handful are new hires within their first 30 days. Dwayne Ellison, the caregiver on visit #41882, is a full-time aide with 38 hours scheduled this week and 11 primary clients.

entities.name: Clients
entities.realism_notes: About 75% Medicaid waiver clients and 25% private pay; authorized hours run 6-35 per week; most have a signed plan of care on file within the last 6 months. Client H. Pruitt is the edge case: authorized_hours_per_week 20, program Medicaid waiver, plan_of_care_on_file true, address_updated_date 3 months ago, and the address still points at the apartment the client left two weeks ago, which is the root cause of the geofence flag on visit #41882.

entities.name: Visit notes
entities.realism_notes: Two to three notes per flagged or cleared visit, timestamps relative to the visit date, in plain operational language ('Called caregiver, left voicemail', 'Family confirmed 4 hours by phone', 'Aggregator file re-pulled, clock-out still missing'). Note types are call, family contact, correction, and system.

edges.label: Drafts a plain-language reason for each mismatch
Approved visits in the Friday claim batch

compliance_notes: Visit and client data would be encrypted at rest and in transit
EVV records would be retained for the state's required retention period and exported in the state's mandated file format
Caregivers see only the clients assigned to them; coordinators see only the clients they manage
Every exception decision is written to an append-only audit log with the coordinator's name and timestamp
Any AI-assisted explanation of an exception runs under a signed BAA; no client PHI is sent to a model without one
No visit reaches the claim batch or the pay run without explicit coordinator approval

design.rationale: Teal with a muted gold accent reads as a home care agency rather than a hospital system, and a serif heading over a humanist sans keeps a dense visit table comfortable for staff who work in it all day.
